detailed_description:
Photorealistic imagery with natural indoor lighting, strong spatial depth, and speed-dependent motion blur.
[Shot 1] Begin exactly from <Picture 1>. In one uninterrupted take, the camera pursues the small fly from <Picture 3>. Use the supplied refmods to preserve the room and its spatial layout.

Keep the fly at realistic housefly scale. It occupies only a small fraction of the image, even during closer passes. Its apparent size varies with distance while remaining a tiny insect within the room.

The fly continually approaches and recedes from the camera. It accelerates ahead and becomes smaller, then follows a tight curved trajectory that briefly brings it closer before it darts away again. Repeat these changes in depth throughout the chase. The camera responds with a slight delay and varies its pursuit speed, allowing the distance to open and close naturally.

The fly shifts freely between the left and right outer thirds, rises toward the upper frame, and drops toward the lower corners. It briefly approaches the frame edges during sudden turns. It crosses the center only momentarily. Avoid fixed central framing, automatic recentering, and a constant tracking distance.

The flight links tight, sharply banked turns with fast sweeping curves around the desktop computer and nearby furniture. The camera accelerates behind the fly and rolls into each turn, with strong parallax as nearby surfaces rush past.

The fly makes a fast airborne pass beside the cat referenced in <Picture 2>. As it crosses within reach, the cat lifts a front paw and swats beside the moving fly, narrowly missing it. At that exact moment, the fly makes one sharp evasive bank and immediately accelerates across the room toward the open storage wardrobe from <Picture 4>. The camera turns after it a fraction later, leaving the cat behind.

As the fly approaches the wardrobe, it pulls farther away from the camera and becomes visibly smaller. It heads directly into the exposed middle shelf compartment containing the stacked light wood boxes and gray case. It crosses behind the front edge of the shelf and flies through the available airspace above and beside these objects, toward the shaded back of that same compartment. The horizontal shelves remain solid boundaries; the fly follows the actual gaps between the stored objects.

The camera approaches the wardrobe more slowly, keeping the shelf opening visible while the tiny fly recedes inside. The wardrobe retains the shallow interior, shelf spacing, clutter, lower drawers, and partly open gray sliding door shown in <Picture 4>. The ending clearly shows the fly entering the shelf compartment and continuing airborne inside it.

The fly remains airborne throughout the entire shot. No landing, perching, resting, or contact with the cat, furniture, shelves, or stored objects. Maintain physically connected trajectories, clear obstacle avoidance, stable room geometry, and continuous momentum, with no cuts.

overall_soundscape:
Natural fly buzzing that grows louder during closer passes and softer as the fly pulls away, subtle indoor ambience, and a brief soft rustle as the cat swats.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
